rationale: The student focuses on individual high digits (9s) rather than comparing digits starting from the highest place value (thousands). A place-value comparison demonstration will explicitly show comparing from the greatest place value first.
intent: Demonstrate compare on the place-value with values [2999,3001]. Tutor points at: the thousands column

frames.caption: Line up 2,999 and 3,001 by place. Start with the biggest place.
3 thousands is more than 2 thousands, so 3,001 is greater than 2,999. The smaller places cannot catch up, even if they are 9s.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration directly tackles the misconception that having 'nines' makes a number larger, explicitly explaining that 3 thousands beats 2 thousands and smaller places cannot catch up even if they are 9s. It uses an analogous pair (2,999 vs 3,001) rather than spoiling 3,999 vs 4,001, providing a clear worked example on a place-value chart.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this is an excellent worked demo that specifically targets the 'more nines' misconception using an isomorphic example.
